items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Great, great saxophone player. Out of Oklahoma City. He died recently in Detroit.

ctx.x: No, I imagine that strikes me as being correct. And I'm in the same, I'm thinking the same way that you think.

Well very often we do think the same way. Good or bad? Both things. Because if I can't keep up with you, you've got too much depth. Now a man that we've mentioned when the date machine went on, was Alvin Walls.
Great, great saxophone player. Out of Oklahoma City. He died recently in Detroit.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Might have been Alvin Walls. ... He's a great, great alto player and a great writer.

ctx.x: Did he play with any other bands?

Yes, I got it. When he came to Dallas, the day that we first arrived in Dallas, and he asked for a job here, he had just left a band out of Oklahoma City, but I don't remember what was the name of the band. Might have been Alvin Walls. See, he died. That was another one of the West Texas, I mean, Western bands. Midwest bands. Alvin Walls. Oh, yeah. He's a great, great alto player and a great writer.
